instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the noodles.
Meanwhile, whisk together 1/4 cup oyster sauce, 3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tbsp sugar in a small bowl. This is the sauce.

Thinly shred about a quarter of the cabbage, enough for 3 cups. Peel the carrot and cut it into thin matchsticks. Mince the 3 garlic cloves. Cut 4 of the green onions into 1 inch pieces, keeping the white and green parts apart.
Slice the 1 lb chicken breasts into strips about 1/4 inch thick. Pat them dry and sprinkle them with the 1/4 tsp salt.
Cook the 12 oz noodles in the boiling water for 1 minute less than the package says. Drain them, rinse them under cold water and shake off as much water as you can.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Add the chicken in one layer and leave it for 2 minutes, until it's golden underneath. Stir it and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until it's golden all over.
You're cooking the chicken to 160°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest strip. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left. Move it to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan with the cabbage, carrot and white parts of the green onions. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until the cabbage softens and turns a little see-through.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the noodles and chicken. Stir the sauce, pour it over and toss everything with tongs for about 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens and coats the noodles.
Toss in the green parts of the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Serve it hot, straight from the pan.
method_notes: All three brown thin strips of chicken, stir-fry cabbage, carrot and green onion with garlic, then toss in boiled chow mein noodles with a soy and oyster sauce mixture. Natasha's Kitchen, the lead, sears the chicken first and sets it aside, and makes the sauce with chicken broth, cornstarch, sugar and 3 tbsp of untoasted sesame oil. RecipeTin Eats marinates the chicken in a spoonful of the sauce, adds Chinese cooking wine and bean sprouts, and stir-fries everything in under 5 minutes, and Once Upon a Chef adds celery and browns the vegetables for 8 minutes. This one follows Natasha's amounts for 4 and uses 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil, as Once Upon a Chef does.
